newsitem.title: USA: Bodyguard says gave drug money to Mexican official.
newsitem.headline: Bodyguard says gave drug money to Mexican official.

text.p: A former bodyguard for a Mexican police commander said on Wednesday he gave two suitcases full of drug money to Mario Ruiz Massieu in a 1994 rendezvous outside the Mexican attorney general's headquarters in Mexico City.

Also, a U.S. Customs agent testified in the civil trial of Ruiz Massieu that informants said the former Mexican deputy attorney general had taken bribes from powerful drug lords, including Amado Carrillo Fuentes.
Ruiz Massieu smiled and shook his head in disgust when the bodyguard, Raul Macias, pointed him out in federal court as the man who got the suitcases loaded with U.S. dollars.

U.S. prosecutors are attempting to confiscate a $9 million Texas bank account belonging to Ruiz Massieu. They charge he got the money from drug-traffickers but he said it was family money placed in Texas Commerce Bank for safekeeping.

Macias told a five-man, three-woman jury he was with a group of federal judicial police officers who unloaded 10 tons of Colombian cocaine from a large plane at a remote airstrip in northern Mexico in August 1994.

Macias, now a government informant, said his boss, local police commander Jesus David Grajera Lara, gave him two suitcases after the incident and put him in a hotel in the city of Zacatecas. While he waited, Macias said, he opened the bags and found them stacked with U.S. dollars, $100,000 of which he took for himself.

The following day he and Grajera Lara went to Mexico City where, after another night in a hotel, they drove to the attorney general's headquarters in the heart of the Mexican capital. There, waiting for them, was a dark blue Ford Grand Marquis.

Inside the car, he said, "there was a driver I did not know and Mr. Ruiz Massieu," whom he recognised from photographs in Grajera Lara's office. Macias said Grajera Lara got out of their car, went over to Ruiz Massieu and made a signal, then had Macias take the two suitcases and place them in the trunk of the Ford.
Macias first testified he was a federal judicial police officer but under questioning by defence attorney Tony Canales he admitted he was only a bodyguard for Grajera Lara.

Also on Wednesday, U.S. Customs agent Robert Rutt testified that, according to informants, Carrillo Fuentes, Mexico's most wanted drug kingpin and head of the powerful Juarez cartel, funnelled money to Ruiz Massieu via the former head of the Mexican federal judicial police, Adrian Carrera Fuentes.

"They would pay it to Adrian Carrera Fuentes, who in turn would give it to Mario Ruiz Massieu," Rutt said. The money was delivered at night to Ruiz Massieu's home, then taken to a safe place by his assistant Jorge Stergios, he said.
Stergios would eventually bring the money to Houston and place it in Ruiz Massieu's bank account, he said.
